# std.validate

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Validation rules: one place to state what a valid value is.

A rule pairs a condition with the error it reports. `validate` returns
the first violation; `validate_all` collects every violation, so a
caller can report all the problems at once.

```badger
validate(book, [
    validate.rule(!text.is_empty(book.title), "title is required"),
    validate.rule(book.title.len() <= 200, "title is too long"),
])
```

## Types

### `Rule`

```badger
pub type Rule<E> = (Bool, E)
```

A rule: a condition and the error it reports when it fails.

### `rule`

### `validate`

```badger
fn validate<T, E>(value: T, rules: List<Rule<E>>) -> Result<T, E>
```

The value when every rule holds; the first failing rule's error
otherwise.

### `validate_all`

```badger
fn validate_all<T, E>(value: T, rules: List<Rule<E>>) -> Result<T, List<E>>
```

The value when every rule holds; every failing rule's error otherwise,
in rule order.
